slides.title: Tripwire / Driftwire
slides.notes: Pinned source; isolated tests and detailed limits in TESTS.md. No hosted demo or official score.

slides.title: 1 · Insufficient samples are checked after the unaffected branch
slides.fix: Evaluate insufficiency before the unaffected return, or return separate compatibility and adequacy results with an explicit trusted-baseline requirement.
slides.notes: A corrected, well-formed four-sample release passed through the full check API: release verdict and A1/A2 were Ready, while the ER-protein question correctly returned Insufficient Evidence. A 40-sample control returned Ready for that question. This confirms the separate meanings of compatibility and question adequacy; it does not invalidate the question-readiness checks.

slides.title: 2 · Decisions recorded is not concerns resolved
slides.fix: Track unresolved findings separately from recorded repair decisions.
slides.notes: Two local browser paths show zero open: request more evidence on a repair, and schema-valid import of a review-required finding with no repair. Exports preserve the decisions/flag. No repair approval or application is claimed.

slides.title: 3 · Analysis rounding precedes effect classification
slides.fix: Keep full-precision calculation fields and format separate display values.
slides.notes: A synthetic increase of 0.0004 in every positive-group measurement left the rounded mean and difference unchanged. a1_compare reported moved=False and 0.0% relative change. The full check API still returned Conditional because its input-level detector caught the change; this is an effect-precision limitation, not a demonstrated overall Ready bypass.

slides.title: 4 · New review calls replace prior decisions
slides.fix: Retain a timestamped history as well as the current decision.
slides.notes: Two apply_decisions calls (approve, then reject) retained one latest decision rather than two events. The original first-returned object was unchanged. This verifies snapshot semantics, not an immutable history.

slides.title: 5 · The no-AI statement is broader than the repository
slides.fix: Scope the claim to the deterministic core and explain the optional intake route, transmitted metadata, and opt-in control.
slides.notes: With consent=False, suggest_mappings raised ValueError before the mocked transport was called. Zero provider calls occurred. This confirms the consent guard; the remaining issue is the README blanket claim.

slides.title: What is verified so far
slides.fix: Read TESTS.md for skips, positive controls and limits.
slides.notes: 404 submitted tests passed, one skipped. Twelve of thirteen local browser checks met reviewer-proposed safeguards. Actual export validator and failed-replacement clearing passed; review-counter concern remained. No hosted/clinical/accessibility certification. The same 404 passed/one skipped under Python 3.13 and declared direct requirements. Separate importer checks: four met, one unmet; corroborates issue 2.
